- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (≥1.5% from prior high), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 0.8–1.2% for 2–3 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bearish to bullish mid-horizon (e.g., +0.33 to +0.67), model lags in adjusting; add 0.3–0.7% upward bias to forecast from day 10 onward.
- When news volume drops below 3.0 for 2+ consecutive days, model underreacts; increase forecast by 0.2–0.5% to compensate for reduced market noise.
- Mean reversion occurs when sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) for 5+ days; model tends to overreact; apply 0.5–1.0% downward correction if price is above 10-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period spikes (last 7–10 days); add 0.3–0.8% upward bias if sentiment is bullish and price is rising.
